definition: Rubinstein–Taybi syndrome is a chromosomal disorder marked by intellectual disability together with distinctive physical differences such as broad thumbs, finger and toe webbing, characteristic facial features, and a range of possible brain, heart, skeletal, breathing, skin, and bowel abnormalities. It follows an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern and is associated with deletion on the short arm of chromosome 16 (16p13.3).
